CanBeGeneratedInCombat.rationale: `=> false` (Feed.cs:18) == the class attribute, with the sim's comment naming the same FilterForCombat consumers. Contrast card/disintegration, where this exact override was mapped to the wrong flag.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Feed.cs:30-33) == cost 1 / ATTACK / RARE / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(10m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new MaxHpVar(3m)` (Feed.cs:20-24) == both numbers, both declared. Powered damage on both sides.

OnPlay.issue: The damage and the max-HP amount are faithful, and so is the max-HP verb's shape: `CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp(Owner.Creature, MaxHp.IntValue)` is `SetMaxHp(MaxHp + amount)` followed by `Heal(num)` (CreatureCmd.cs:786-799) == the sim's `ctx.player.max_hp += self._max_hp` then `CreatureCmd.heal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self._max_hp)`. THE FATAL TEST IS NOT. C# computes `bool shouldTriggerFatal = cardPlay.Target.Powers.All(p => p.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal())` BEFORE the attack (Feed.cs:38) and only grants max HP when that is true AND the attack actually killed (`attackCommand.Results...Any(r => r.WasTargetKilled)`, line 42). The sim tests only `if target.is_dead` (feed.py:45), dropping the power-veto half entirely. Two C# powers return false from `ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal`: `MinionPower` (unconditionally, MinionPower.cs:20-23) and `ReattachPower` (unless every other segment is dead, ReattachPower.cs:106-109). BOTH ARE PORTED -- `MinionPower` at powers.py:1536-1542, applied by three ported monsters (`monsters/glory/fabricator.py:182`, `monsters/glory/queen.py:50`, `monsters/hive/ovicopter.py:128`), and ReattachPower at powers.py:2360. Observable: kill a Fabricator bot, a Queen minion or an Ovicopter egg with Feed -- the game grants NO max HP, the sim grants 3 and heals 3. LIVE. The sim's docstring (feed.py:17-19) claims the Illusion case "falls out of the is_dead check", which is true for DEATH PREVENTION but does not cover the fatal-veto powers, which allow the death and only suppress the Fatal trigger. RATIONALE CITES THIRD FILES (rule 7): MinionPower.cs, ReattachPower.cs, CreatureCmd.cs, powers.py and the three monster modules are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: `WasTargetKilled` vs the sim's `target.is_dead` for the KILL half of the test (Feed.cs:42)
guards.rationale: These agree: the target is chosen from living enemies, so `is_dead` after the single hit means this attack killed it, and a death-prevention effect leaves it alive on both sides (the sim floors a saved creature at 1 HP, cmds.py:106-112). The divergence is entirely in the missing power veto, which the OnPlay entry owns.
